Package com.egradx.auth.entity

Class EgradxOrganizationMembershipEntity

java.lang.Object
com.egradx.auth.entity.EgradxOrganizationMembershipEntity
@Entity public class EgradxOrganizationMembershipEntity extends Object
The row that actually answers "what role does this user have in this organization" — a user can belong to several organizations, but this table's (userId, organizationId) unique constraint enforces exactly one role per organization per user. Plain UUID columns rather than @ManyToOne associations, matching this module's existing style (see EgradxUserEntity.primaryAccountId) and keeping this table decoupled from needing to load the full user/organization/role graph just to answer a membership question.

Administering the platform is a membership like any other — of the platform organization. This previously used organizationId == null for that case, which meant the unique constraint didn't actually constrain it: most databases don't treat multiple NULLs as duplicates, so nothing stopped a user accumulating several "platform" rows. With the platform being a real organization, the constraint applies to it like everything else.

roleId must reference a role belonging to this same organizationId — enforced in EgradxRoleService/ EgradxOrganizationMembershipService at write time, not by a DB constraint (a role and its organization live in different tables with no natural FK to express "same org as this membership row").
